flag.name: Flag of Arkansas
flag.description: A rectangular field of red, on which is placed a large white diamond, bordered by a wide band of blue on which are twenty-five white stars, with one star above and three stars below the word 'ARKANSAS.'
flag.symbolism: The diamond represents Arkansas' natural diamonds. 25 white stars represent Arkansas' admittance to the Union as the 25th state. The star above 'ARKANSAS' represents the Confederacy. The three stars below 'ARKANSAS' represent the three nations which have owned Arkansas: France, Spain, and the United States; as well as Arkansas' formation as the third state from the Louisiana Purchase. Two of the stars in the flag are said to represent Arkansas and Michigan as twin states, their acts of admission being signed on the same day.

seal.name: Great Seal of Arkansas
seal.description: An eagle at the bottom, holding a scroll in its beak, inscribed 'Regnat populus,' a bundle of arrows in one claw and an olive branch in the other; a shield covering the breast of the eagle, engraved with a steamboat at top, a beehive and plow in the middle, and sheaf of wheat at the bottom; the Goddess of Liberty at the top, holding a wreath in her right hand, a pole in the left hand, surmounted by a liberty cap, and surrounded by a circle of stars outside of which is a circle of rays; the figure of an angel on the left, inscribed 'Mercy,' and a sword in the right hand, inscribed 'Justice,' surrounded with the words 'Seal of the State of Arkansas.'

symbols.creed: I believe in Arkansas as a land of opportunity and promise. I believe in the rich heritage of Arkansas and I honor the men and women who created this heritage. I believe in the youth of Arkansas who will build our future. I am proud of my state, I will uphold its constitution, obey its laws, and work for the good of all its citizens.
symbols.fruit and vegetable: South Arkansas vine ripe pink tomato
symbols.quarter: State quarter featuring diamond, rice stalks, and mallard flying above a lake.
